title: Block-sparse hybrid attention kernel with fused rotary and KV-shard scheduler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce an optional block-sparse attention kernel with fused rotary embeddings and a KV-shard-aware scheduler. Improves 90th percentile throughput on long-context chat workloads by up to 2.2x and reduces tail latency under contention. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via runtime config 'attn.kernel=block_sparse'.
description: Context: some production workloads (document-search chat and long-history assistants) show poor GPU utilization for large sequence lengths due to dense attention compute and memory-bound KV cache shuffles. This PR introduces a hybrid block-sparse attention microkernel plus a KV-shard scheduler that routes KV cache slices to co-located warps to reduce cross-SM memory traffic. The work also fuses the rotary/rope transform into the attention microkernel to avoid an extra memory pass. Design summary: - Block-sparse microkernel that partitions QKV into fixed-size blocks (64x64 / 128x128) and executes fused QK/softmax/V matmuls when dense blocks are present; falls back to a fast dense path for short sequences. - In-kernel rotary/rope application fused in-place into the Q/K compute to remove an additional kernel launch and memory write. Supports interleaved rotary for both single-head and multi-head layouts. - KV-shard scheduler in the runtime that pins KV shards by sequence-range and places requests with overlapping prefixes onto the same GPU stream/SM affinity group to maximize KV cache locality. - Continuous-batcher aware: kernel adds lightweight metadata to allow the batcher to coalesce blocks across requests with similar start offsets. Benchmarks (internal synthetic and canary on dedicated pool): - 2.2x throughput improvement for 8k context long-chat benchmark (N=32 concurrent streams) vs current main: 2.2x median throughput, 1.9x 95p. - 1.35x improvement on mixed short/long workload (50% <512, 50% 6k) in P99 latency under load. - CPU scheduling overhead increased by ~3% due to shard-placement bookkeeping; net cost justified by GPU gains. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA) with unit-tested math kernels - [x] Runtime scheduler + fallback heuristics - [x] Integration tests against existing KV cache invariants - [x] Microbench harness + perf dashboards updated - [x] Canary rollout plan and abort thresholds documented Migration notes: - Feature is opt-in via runtime config 'attn.kernel=block_sparse' (default remains 'flash'). - For Dedicated customers, recommend enabling on a small percentage of nodes behind A/B rollout. - No model change required. Related: design doc at docs/design/attn/block_sparse_hybrid.md, perf dashboard run: perf/dashboards/block_sparse_oct2024.

review_conversation: Diego Alvarez: Initial pass looks good. Two questions: (1) can you explain the choice of block sizes and whether we expose that as a knob? (2) We need to ensure deterministic results for model evals when switching kernels.

Maya Chen: Reply: block sizes selected after sweep (64/128) — added config 'attn.block_size' with safe defaults and auto-tuner stub; deterministic numerics preserved by forcing same FP accumulation order in fused path (see block_sparse_kernel.h comments).
Priya Nair: Please add a fallback to dense path if block sparsity ratio < 10% to avoid worst-case regression on very dense attention patterns.
Maya Chen: Added heuristic and test (will fallback when sparsity < 12%).
Omar Hassan: CI flagged a flaky test in continuous_batcher; looks like a race on stream fences
Maya Chen: Fixed with explicit stream synch on the coalesce path and added stress test. Re-ran CI; all green.
merge_outcome: Merged after addressing reviewer feedback and adding fallback heuristics. Canary ran for 48h on Dedicated pool with no regressions and a 1.9-2.2x sustained throughput improvement for targeted workloads. Rolled out as opt-in config with auto-rollback thresholds.
bench_summary: 8k context, batch size 32: median throughput +2.2x, 95p +1.9x. Mixed workload P99 latency -26% under 75% load. Memory footprint: KV cache shard locality reduces global traffic by ~18% in canary traces.
